summary.headline: PNB Housing Q1 FY27 PAT rose 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA 2.37% and ROE 11.44%, while NIM fell 19 bps QoQ to 3.50%.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 PAT grew 4% YoY to INR 557 crore, with ROA of 2.37% and ROE of 11.44%. Disbursements moved to a cheque-realisation basis this quarter, so reported disbursement grew 18% YoY to INR 5,882 crore against 56% on the old cheque-handover basis. Loan book grew 15% YoY to INR 89,670 crore, NIM moderated to 3.50% and gross NPA was 0.95%. Management says margin and yield have bottomed and expects Q2 to be much better than Q1, especially in Affordable.

financial_highlights.change: -19 bps QoQ (12 bps leverage, 7 bps Q4 true-up)

financial_highlights.metric: Spread / portfolio yield / cost of borrowing
financial_highlights.change: Spread stable QoQ; yield +1 bp; cost of borrowing +1 bp

financial_highlights.value: Negative 12 bps (recoveries INR 67 crore from written-off pool)

segments.name: Prime
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 3,083 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; Prime yield up about 8 bps QoQ, which management attributes mostly to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans.

segments.name: Emerging Markets
segments.commentary: Disbursement INR 2,029 crore in Q1 FY27, double-digit YoY growth; INR 71 crore disbursed under the new Emerging Developer Finance programme.

segments.name: Affordable / Emerging (retail)
segments.commentary: Affordable and Emerging book grew 27% YoY and is 41% of retail portfolio (target 45% by FY27-end). Affordable net disbursement only INR 555 crore, below target; management cites about 11% YoY growth on a like-for-like basis.

segments.name: Corporate loan book
segments.commentary: INR 493 crore outstanding at 30 June 2026, with about INR 215 crore disbursed in Q1 FY27.

segments.name: Written-off pool (retail)
segments.commentary: About INR 340 crore remaining; INR 67 crore recovered in Q1. One legacy account of about INR 420 crore was classified as fraud, already fully provided in FY23, so no incremental P&L impact.

guidance_outlook: Full-year FY27 overall loan book growth guidance of 18% to 20% maintained; management says it expects to beat it.
Affordable loan book growth guidance of 50% to 60% maintained for FY27.
Construction finance capped at about 3% of the overall book in FY27.
Affordable and Emerging share to reach 45% of book by FY27-end and about 50% in FY28.
FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 ROA around 2.3% as credit cost normalises. Long-term ROA 2.3% to 2.35%.
NIM expected to have bottomed; gradual improvement from H2 FY27. Yield expected to keep improving on mix.
Credit cost expected to stay negative through FY27 on continued recoveries.
Q2 FY27 disbursement (net) expected 60% to 70% above Q1 overall and 2.5x to 2.6x in Affordable; management says July was promising.
Rating upgrades (CARE done; ICRA and CRISIL pending) expected to cut cost of borrowing by at least about 10 bps.
capex_capacity: Branch network expanded by 12 in the quarter to 404 branches.
Affordable business launched from selected Prime and Emerging branches; about INR 30 crore disbursed in June, and 15% to 18% of Affordable business in July.
Management does not plan to open more branches; plans to use existing branches to contain opex.
Micro-housing policy formulated and rolled out in Q2 FY27; meaningful contribution expected from H2 FY27.
Full buyout transactions started; loan assets of INR 146 crore acquired in Q1 FY27.
demand_pricing: Management cites steady housing demand across retail mortgage segments, particularly Affordable and Emerging Markets; RBI repo unchanged at 5.25%.
Gross disbursement YoY growth of 56% on cheque-handover basis vs 18% on the new net basis; the gap reflects the accounting change, not lost demand.
Incremental disbursement yield is above the 9.48% book yield, per management.
Incremental cost of borrowing rose about 18 bps in Q1 on tighter liquidity and market volatility; management says it has eased somewhat but remains elevated.
BT-in share of sourcing fell to 4.4% from 5% a year ago; Affordable BT-in fell to 3.4% from 10.5%.
Prime yield mix benefit about 10 to 15 bps; Affordable yield up about 50 bps QoQ per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should yield and cost of funds trend, and does the medium-term NIM expansion thesis from mix shift toward Affordable/Emerging/CF still hold over two years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said margin, yield and cost of funds have all bottomed; gradual margin improvement expected from H2 FY27. Construction finance capped at 3% of book in FY27; Affordable and Emerging share at 41% now, targeting 45% by FY27-end and nearly 50% in two years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the gross disbursement momentum (55%+ on cheque-handover basis) carry into Q2 and make the 18-20% loan growth guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management aims to beat both gross and net Q2 numbers, said Q2 gross will be much better than Q1 and July showed strong gross and net momentum. It said it expects to do much better than the 18-20% loan growth guidance but did not raise it.

qa_highlights.question: Why did leverage and NII move sharply when debt-to-equity barely changed?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said average leverage rose from 3.6x to 3.75x; Q4 disbursement realisations flowed into Q1 borrowings, and lower investment yields also weighed on total yield.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gap between reported and gross disbursement across all segments, and what is Affordable growth on a like-for-like basis?
qa_highlights.answer: The gap spans Prime, Emerging and Affordable since retail and wholesale moved to debit-from-account recognition. Like-for-like Affordable YoY growth is about 11%.

qa_highlights.question: Will credit cost turn positive in H2, and what ROA path follows?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said credit cost should stay negative through FY27 given line of sight on recoveries. FY27 ROA guided around 2.4%; FY28 around 2.3% as credit cost normalises; long-term 2.3% to 2.35%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did recoveries of about INR 77 crore not fully flow through ECL writeback, and where did the difference go?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO said regular OTS settlements cost about INR 10-12 crore, booked as write-offs in Prime and Emerging legacy pool, explaining the gap versus the INR 67 crore recovery figure.

qa_highlights.question: What is Q2 net disbursement growth versus Q1 net, and what does July look like?
qa_highlights.answer: Overall Q2 net disbursement expected about 60-70% above Q1 net; Affordable 2.5x-2.6x Q1 net. Management said July was promising, with Prime and Emerging contributing 15-18% of Affordable business in July.

qa_highlights.question: How much benefit from rating upgrades and when will it show in cost of borrowing?
qa_highlights.answer: CARE upgrade is done; ICRA and CRISIL pending. CFO said at least about 10 bps reduction in cost of borrowing should come through; some fresh borrowing already at better rates.

qa_highlights.question: Prime yield rose 8 bps: how much is mix versus like-for-like, and does self-employed mix raise risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed about 10-15 bps benefit to mix shift toward self-employed and non-home loans; without mix, Prime yield would have been roughly stable at 8.92-8.95%. Delinquency in Prime and Emerging said to have improved QoQ.

risks_watch: Affordable execution: Q1 net disbursement of INR 555 crore is below target; Q2 needs 2.5-2.6x Q1 net and 50-60% full-year Affordable growth is guided, with new CBO leadership still unproven.

Cost of borrowing: incremental cost rose about 18 bps in Q1 and management says it is still elevated; the NIM bottoming thesis depends on yield gains offsetting this plus further leverage increase (average 3.6x to 3.75x).
Rating upgrades: ICRA and CRISIL still pending; management expects at least 10 bps cost-of-funds benefit, timing not firm.
Credit cost: negative 12 bps in Q1 relies on written-off pool recoveries (INR 67 crore) that will shrink from about INR 340 crore; sustainability of negative credit cost beyond FY27 is open.
Fraud account of about INR 420 crore: fully provided in FY23, but recovery timing and quantum not guided; management declined to quantify expected FY27 recoveries.
Disbursement realisation under cheque-realisation accounting: management expects the transition to flow through over about two months, so Q2 reported figures depend on timing of realisations.
key_quotes: Yes, I think if I talk about Q2, I think we will try to beat both the numbers, which is gross or net.
So I think 18 to 20%, that's the guidance which we are going to definitely, our team is focusing on better growth than what we have given guidance.
Going forward, we feel NIM has largely bottomed out and should start improving from second half of this financial year.
So it was an artificial lift in NIM in Q4, whereas that start getting normalized from Q1 onwards.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the medium-term margin, yield and disbursement recovery, with repeated claims that margin, yield and cost of funds have bottomed and that July was strong. Cautious on specifics: management did not give exact Q2 figures, declined to quantify recoveries on the fraud account, and called incremental cost of borrowing still elevated.
